channel.name: Krishna Universe
channel.niche: Bhagwan Shri Krishna ki leelayein aur unse milne wali seekh
channel.tagline: Roz ek katha, roz ek seekh
channel.url_note: PLACEHOLDER. Replace with the real channel handle - it is printed in every description, so a wrong handle sends viewers nowhere.

video.min_duration_note: HARD FLOOR - a Short must never come out under 25s. video_composer clamps the timeline to this, so a short narration is padded rather than published short. But padding leaves trailing silence, so gemini.min_words below makes the NARRATION long enough in the first place; the clamp is only the safety net.
video.cut_note: Shortened from 2.6/1.6. With ~30s of runtime this takes the reel from ~12 visual changes to ~16. Combined with every shot now carrying a zoom (see motion below), that is what removes the slideshow feel - a slow cut on a barely-moving frame is what makes a still look like a still.
video.encode_note: crf 18 -> 16 and preset medium -> slow. YouTube re-encodes anyway, so the only thing under our control is how much detail survives INTO their encoder. A lower crf on a grainy, high-motion 1080x1920 source measurably preserves more. Costs render time, not quality.
video.comment_duration: 30s as requested. A Hindi katha needs the extra seconds the parent channel did not - the leela has to land AND the seekh has to be stated, and 24s forces one of them out.
video.comment_cuts: TWO cut lengths now. scene_cut_seconds is how long a generated Krishna frame holds; clip_cut_seconds is the shorter beat for real atmosphere footage cut in between. The real shots are kept shorter so they read as accents, not as the subject.

motion.comment: The anti-slideshow settings. overscan is how much larger than the frame each still is rendered, which is the travel room a pan has - at 1.0 nothing can move and the result IS a slideshow. real_every controls the mix: after this many generated frames, one REAL moving shot is cut in.
motion.overscan_note: Lowered 1.28 -> 1.18. Overscan is upscaling: at 1.28 a generated frame had to be enlarged 28% before any panning, and that softness was visible. 18% still leaves real travel room while keeping the image crisp. ai_images now delivers frames AT this size, pre-sharpened, so nothing is upscaled at render time.
motion.zoom_note: Raised 0.10 -> 0.16, and every move now carries a zoom rather than 8 of 10 being pure pans. A 10% drift over 2.6s is below the threshold where the eye reads it as camera movement.

ai_images.comment: This is the visual layer. There is no real footage of Krishna anywhere, so each story beat is generated from the ENGLISH scene prompts gemini_script requests alongside the narration. Vertical (1080x1920) on purpose - generating 16:9 and cropping would cut the crown off the top of every frame.
ai_images.dimension_note: NOT the final frame size. 1080x1920 is 2.07 MP at a 0.5625 aspect, well past the ~1 MP the model is trained on, and asking for both produced visibly STRETCHED figures - wide faces, broad bodies. 1024x1792 is 1.83 MP at 0.5714, close enough to 9:16 that almost nothing is cropped, and inside the range where anatomy stays correct. ai_images._postprocess() then upscales to the overscan size with LANCZOS and an unsharp mask.
ai_images.style: cinematic indian mythological art, dramatic warm lighting, rich saffron and deep blue palette, highly detailed, volumetric god rays, soft film grain, painterly, devotional, beautiful
ai_images.style_note: One house style across all 150 leelas. Without it every upload arrives in a different art style, which is what makes an AI channel look like a random image dump rather than a channel.

transitions.comment: Shorter than the parent channel's 0.3s. With cuts every ~1.6-2.6s a long crossfade eats a real fraction of each shot and softens the pace.

palette.comment: Saffron / gold / deep indigo - devotional, not pastel.

captions.comment: OFF, matching the owner's decision on the parent channel: the rolling word-by-word track with a dark pill behind it looked cluttered and covered the subject. Do NOT switch this on without asking. Muted viewers are served by flash_text instead. NOTE: the 'font' key here is now ignored - all text goes through modules/textrender.py, which resolves a Devanagari font itself.

flash_text.comment: Three short Hindi phrases (2-4 words) appear for ~1.4s each in the UPPER third, no backdrop panel, soft fade. Gives a muted viewer something to read without covering the scene. Slightly longer and slightly smaller than the parent channel's: Devanagari takes more horizontal room per word and needs a beat longer to read than English.

hook.comment: Short 2-4 word Hindi label from pools.SCREEN_HOOKS for the first 2.5s. fontsize reduced 118 -> 100: Devanagari has matras above and conjuncts below the baseline, so the same point size occupies noticeably more vertical space than Latin and 118 pushed 2-line hooks off frame.
hook.strength_note: Made deliberately harder: bigger text, faster snap-in, a stronger overshoot and a real background punch. The previous values were so gentle that the opening did not register as a hook at all - which was the feedback.

grain.comment: A faint moving grain layer over the whole reel. Generated frames are unnaturally clean - no sensor noise, no texture - and that cleanliness is a big part of why animated stills read as a slideshow. Grain gives every frame something that changes even when the camera move is slow. Rendered at 1/6 scale and enlarged so it stays soft rather than becoming a pixel fizz.

cta_overlay.comment: LIKE / SHARE / SUBSCRIBE over the last few seconds. The narration already ends with a spoken sign-off, but a viewer watching on mute never hears it - and the end of a Short is exactly when someone who enjoyed it decides whether to act. Nothing on screen was asking them to.
cta_overlay.subtext: कमेंट में लिखिए — जय श्री कृष्ण 🙏

tts.comment: HINDI voices. Madhur (male) leads because a katha-vachak reading suits this niche and is what the audience expects. The pool is deliberately SMALL - only 2 voices. The parent channel rotates 6, but on a katha channel a returning viewer builds trust with one narrator, and swapping voices daily breaks the only piece of channel identity a faceless channel has. Two is enough to avoid sounding like a single automated template while staying recognisable.
tts.rate_note: Slower than the parent channel. Devotional narration read at conversational speed sounds rushed and disrespectful, and Hindi TTS is harder to follow at speed than English.

gemini.target_words_note: Hindi TTS at -10% rate runs roughly 140 words/min, so 62 words ~= 26.5s and 84 words ~= 36s. min_words is set above the 58 words that 25s strictly needs, because TTS pace varies with sentence length and punctuation - a script sitting exactly on 25s would sometimes land under it. Raising target_words without lowering the rate is what makes a 'Short' overshoot 60s.

seo.comment: Consumed by modules/seo.py. hashtag_count stays under 15 because YouTube ignores ALL hashtags on a video carrying more than 15.

thumbnail.comment: Shorts thumbnails do not show inside the Shorts player, but they ARE the channel grid, the subscriptions feed and search - the surfaces where a viewer decides to subscribe. Text is drawn through textrender so the Hindi caption is shaped correctly.

pexels.comment: ATMOSPHERE ONLY. These are things that genuinely exist on stock video sites - river water, peacocks, cows, diya flames, rain. Krishna himself is never searched for here (there is no such footage); the leela is carried by ai_images. The composer cuts these real moving shots between the generated frames, which is what stops the result reading as a slideshow.

music.comment: Music slightly quieter than the parent channel (0.18 -> 0.16). The narration here carries the whole video and Hindi consonant clusters lose clarity under a busy bed far faster than English does.

grade.comment: Warm, rich, devotional. Vignette OFF (the oval look was rejected on the parent channel).

youtube.category_note: 24 = Entertainment. Devotional storytelling sits here rather than 27 (Education); Entertainment is where this niche's traffic and suggested-video pool actually is.
youtube.language_note: Both language fields matter. Without them YouTube guesses the language from the title, and a Hindi video mislabelled as English is served to the wrong audience and loses auto-translation of the title/description.
youtube.made_for_kids_note: Owner confirmed this channel is NOT made for kids. Marking it as such would disable comments entirely - killing the pinned-comment strategy - and switch off personalised ads, roughly halving RPM.
youtube.default_tags_note: FALLBACK ONLY. modules/seo.py builds a per-video, leela-aware tag set at generate time.
youtube.hashtags_note: FALLBACK ONLY. Per-video rotating hashtags come from modules/seo.py.

instagram.comment: OFF by default - automated IG posting carries account ban risk.

posting_times_ist.comment: India Standard Time targets. IST has NO daylight saving, so unlike the parent channel's US schedule the cron never needs a seasonal correction. Cron in the workflow is UTC = IST - 5:30, set ~80 min EARLIER than the publish target to absorb GitHub's scheduler queue delay plus render time.
